question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Din-i Ilahi.
question.text: The Din-i Ilahi was a new syncretic religion promulgated by Akbar, the ruler of this empire. This Muslim empire ruled over most of India under its last major emperor, Aurangzeb.
question.clue: This empire was antagonized by the Maratha confederacy under Shivaji.

swap.text: Muhammad Ali Jinnah is considered the father of this nation, which split from India in 1947. This nation still disputes the Kashmir province with India.
swap.clue: This nation lost the Bangladesh Liberation War in 1971.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the history of India.
question.text: Name this surname of two Indian leaders, the Prime Minister Indira and the non-violent leader of the Salt March, Mahatma
question.clue: A politician with this surname instituted forced sterilization and removed civil liberties during a period dubbed "The Emergency."

swap.leadin: This man championed a policy of Satyagraha and led the Salt March before being assassinated by Nathuram Godse.
swap.text: Name this Indian nationalist leader, a champion of nonviolent civil disobedience.
swap.clue: As a lawyer, he led a campaign to protest voting restrictions in Natal, South Africa, and he urged the wearing of the namesake cloth in the khadi movement.

question.text: After Pan Am Flight 73 was hijacked on the ground in this country, Gaddafi paid the American victims $150 million. Another act of terrorism saw this country's PM Benazir Bhutto assassinated in 2007.
question.answerHtml: Pakistan [or Islamic Republic of Pakistan or Jamhuryat Islami Pakistan]
question.clue: This country began enriching uranium in response to a neighboring country's Smiling Buddha test.

swap.text: Afonso de Albuquerque conquered this city on India's west coast in 1510. It remained a Portuguese possession until India annexed it in Operation Vijay.
swap.clue: Colony state, which was seized in Operation Vijay, is where Francis Xavier proselytized and is buried.

question.text: This competing empire named for a rebellious caste from a particular state was predominantly Hindu and arose in reaction to Mughal Emperor Aurengzeb's intolerant religious policies. After defeating the Mughals despite losing the Third Battle of Panipat this empire was eventually conquered by the British.
question.clue: The position held by the Bhat family in this empire was that of Peshwa, and that held by Shuha and his grandfather was Chhatrapati.

swap.text: From a human standpoint, probably the worst industrial disaster to date was a 1984 release of toxic methyl isocyanate from a Union Carbide plant in this Indian city.
swap.clue: This city where in 1984, methyl isocyanate leaked from a pesticide plant, causing the deadliest industrial disaster in history.

question.leadin: A 1963 crisis in this region developed after a strand of the Prophet Mohammad's hair was stolen from a shrine in Hazratbal.
question.text: Identify this region claimed by both India and Pakistan on opposite sides of the Line of Control. It should not be confused with Punjab.
question.clue: The Poonch Rebellion preceded the signing of this region's Instrument of Accession by Hari Singh.

swap.leadin: This dynasty reached its peak in the 9th century AD before being overthrown by the Pandyan Dynasty in the 1300s, ending a 1600 year period of rule over South India.
swap.text: The Brihadisvara is one of which dynasty's "Great Living Temples" that it built in its capital of Thanjavur? During the height of its power, it established a maritime empire stretching from the Philippines to the Maldives.
swap.clue: This dynasty conquered the Andaman and (+) Nicobar Islands under Rajendra I, son of Raja Raja I. This dynasty originates from the Sangam Period, as do the Chera and Pandya dynasties.

question.leadin: Identify these events from the British colonization of India.
question.text: Cartridges of Enfield Rifles greased with pork fat incited this uprising in 1857, which began in Meerut after the Bahadur Shah was proclaimed emperor and was put down by Colin Campbell.
question.clue: It was kicked off by the attempted assassinations of Mangal Pandey.

swap.leadin: This group assassinated President Premadasa in 1993.
swap.text: Name this terrorist group that wanted to form a separate state from the rest of the Buddhist Sinhalese population.
swap.answerHtml: Tamil Tigers [or Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam; or LTTE; prompt on Tigers]
swap.clue: This group, based out of Kilinochchi, suffered its final defeat at Mullaitivu.

question.leadin: Immigrants of this nationality were targeted in the 1907 Bellingham Riots.
question.text: Give this nationality of a religious leader who declared "Sisters and brothers of America!" as part of a speech at the Parliament of World Religions that spread awareness of Hinduism to the U.S.

swap.leadin: The "house" named for this country, a former control center for its southern regions, is no longer within its borders thanks to the 1865 Treaty of Sinchula that it signed with Britain.
swap.text: Name this country whose rule by the Wangchuck dynasty, a branch of the long-influential Dorji family, began in 1907 after its reunification.
swap.answerHtml: Bhutan [or Kingdom of Bhutan; or Druk Gyal Kap; accept Bhutan House]
swap.clue: One ruler of this nation used the Tsa Yig legal code to establish a dual system of government.

question.text: In 1993, this third President of Sri Lanka was killed by the Tamil Tigers. He had previously given arms to them to help them rid Sri Lanka of the Indian Peace Keeping Force, but this proved counter-productive.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about homosexuality in medieval India.
swap.text: The Hindu slave Khusrau Khan briefly took this title, succeeding his lover, Qutb-ud-Din. Another holder of this title, Ibrahim Lodi, was defeated at the First Battle of Panipat, and the holders of this title ruled from modern India's capital

question.text: The Amritsar protestors were expressing opposition to these laws, which addressed Indian sedition by removing the rights of warrant, habeas corpus, and appeal from those subject to the British Raj.
question.clue: Also known as the "Black Acts," name this 1919 legislation which was passed over the unanimous opposition of the Indian members of the Supreme Legislative Council.

swap.text: Starting in 1782, this man ruled Mysore. He allied with France and fought three wars against the British, losing badly in the last two. He was killed in 1799 when the British stormed his fortress at Seringapatam.
swap.clue: The V&A owns a wooden automaton commissioned by this man of a creature biting into the neck of a Western soldier.

question.leadin: One apocryphal account in this religion's history holds that the sixty-nine-year-old Baba Deep held his severed head on his body while storming a holy city in 1757.
question.text: Name this religion whose members were massacred in the Chhota and Wadda Holocausts, which occurred in 1746 and 1762 at the hands of Lakhpat Rai and Ahmad Shah Abdali.
question.clue: That monarch who followed this religion defeated the Afghan king Zaman Shah to capture Lahore, then declared himself a maharaja.

swap.text: This Tamil-speaking state was founded by Rajendra I and controlled almost all of eastern India for a time, as well as Malaysia and Sumatra.
swap.clue: Similar theories about the occupation of Northern India often propose that survivors of the Indus Valley Civilization fled South to establish three kingdoms in the Deccan: Chera, Pandya, and this largest Tamil empire.
